rel-037.explanation: MemRL freezes the LLM and learns nonparametric memory utility; MemSkill trains a small MLP selector while revising external skills. Neither makes a called large LLM's weights trainable merely by using it.

rel-038.explanation: Eureka sends policy-training results to a frozen LLM; DERL uses those results to train the reward-design model.

rel-039.explanation: ACE retains experience in context; MASS trains collaborative trajectories into shared weights. The comparison concerns where capability persists.

rel-040.explanation: Harness-R1 trains an editing model using successful reruns; HarnessDev studies generated runtimes and their execution benefits.

rel-041.explanation: Both combine program generation, execution evaluation, and archives. Training and infrastructure applications support AI4AI; general algorithm optimization has a separate target.

rel-042.explanation: EnvHarness edits interaction wrappers to support learning; WebRL organizes failures into a training curriculum.

rel-043.explanation: SkillRL Table 1 compares with MemRL. MemRL learns memory utility with a frozen LLM, whereas SkillRL trains a policy while maintaining skills; the edge records comparison, not code inheritance.

rel-llm-self-improve-rest-em.explanation: ReST-EM compares with Huang et al.'s generated-reasoning training, distinguishing consistency filtering from verifiable task rewards.

rel-meta-harness-evotrainer.explanation: EvoTrainer discusses Meta-Harness, contrasting inference-system configuration search with training-plan improvement guided by actual training outcomes.

industry-metacircle-ophis-recursive-firs.explanation: OPHIS's NanoGPT case starts from Recursive's public solution but changes the evaluation budget, so the scores are not a shared-protocol ranking.

industry-apex-tune-recursive-first-steps.explanation: Apex cites Recursive's public results and notes that some kernel comparisons are not paired measurements on the same machine.

industry-comfyresearch-metacircle-ophis.explanation: ComfyResearch connects its human-directed experiments to the separately developed OPHIS automated loop.

source-rhi-mass-workflow.explanation: MASS Appendix J explicitly credits RHI for workflow search; MASS adds trajectory post-training.

read-levin-tree-search-policy-guided-heu.explanation: Policy-guided heuristic search extends depth-over-policy cost to general node costs and a heuristic factor.

read-policy-guided-heuristic-search-lts-.explanation: LTS with context models retains bootstrap training and the LTS search loss while adopting convexly optimizable context models.

read-alphago-zero-muzero-compares.explanation: MuZero replaces search with exact known rules by learned latent dynamics and supports intermediate rewards.

read-dgm-hgm-extends.explanation: HGM retains self-modifying code lineages while estimating descendant potential through Clade Metaproductivity to allocate budget.

read-opro-promptbreeder-method_compariso.explanation: OPRO discusses Promptbreeder as concurrent mutation/crossover work; OPRO itself keeps the meta-instruction fixed and uses candidate-score history.

read-skill-self-play-skillrl-method_comp.explanation: Skill Self-Play derives skills from failures to structure tasks and verification; SkillRL retrieves and revises skills to guide solving and parameter learning.

read-memskill-skillrl-method_comparison.explanation: MemSkill uses fixed LLMs for skill execution and design while PPO trains a small MLP controller; SkillRL updates the base language model alongside a skill library.

read-envharness-rlanything-method_compar.explanation: EnvHarness mainly improves interaction with a frozen LLM and has a separate 8B training branch; RLAnything jointly updates environment diagnosis, reward signals, and policy RL.

read-star-rest-em-discusses.explanation: ReST-EM explicitly compares with STaR and formulates selected-trajectory supervised updates through EM.

read-rest-em-seal-uses.explanation: SEAL uses ReST-EM to train an editing policy with reward from the learner's post-edit performance.

read-star-absolute-zero-discusses.explanation: Absolute Zero cites STaR as a precursor in verified reasoning self-training and adds automatic task generation.

read-r-zero-agent0-compares.explanation: Agent0 extends R-Zero-style dual-role curricula, answer agreement, and repetition penalties with tool trajectories and ADPO.

read-r-zero-dr-zero-compares.explanation: Dr. Zero extends a zero-label curriculum to retrieval and compares against search-augmented R-Zero; HRPO reduces nested proposer sampling.

read-absolute-zero-tool-r0-compares.explanation: Tool-R0 contrasts its tool-call curriculum with AZR's executable-program environment; its main empirical measure is structural matching.

read-agent0-tool-r0-compares.explanation: Tool-R0 expands from Python reasoning curricula to multi-tool schema prediction without equivalent evidence of real execution success.

read-actor-curator-self-evolving-curricu.explanation: Actor-Curator compares with SEC, replacing absolute-advantage utility with estimated old-to-new policy improvement and selecting individual questions rather than categories.

read-skillos-reasoningbank-compares.explanation: SkillOS holds the executor fixed when comparing learned skill curation with ReasoningBank's experience abstraction.

read-reflexion-reasoningbank.explanation: Both freeze model weights and retain textual experience. Reflexion mainly revises short memory across attempts at one task; ReasoningBank explicitly accumulates strategies across queries.

read-meta-harness-hase.explanation: HASE names Meta-Harness as its closest comparison: one trains a shared solving/editing policy, while the other uses a fixed external coding proposer.

read-hase-mass.explanation: MASS Table 15 compares HASE's shared solving/editing policy with its own skill and model feedback mechanism; the relation does not imply code inheritance.

discovery-loop.name: Discovery Loop
discovery-loop.focus: Automating the full cycle of proposing, implementing, running, interpreting, and revising experiments, initially in ML research and its own technology stack.
discovery-loop.boundary: The public site describes a direction and team; parameter-update schedules, inherited improvers, and multi-generation gains are not yet technically specified. Founders' previous Google work remains attributed to Google.

metacircle.name: MetaCircle
metacircle.focus: Science of AI and AI for AI through training-dynamics observations, mechanism hypotheses, and executable experiments.
metacircle.boundary: The three entries cover automated research, an experiment workbench, and observation resources, with distinct evidence and update objects.

apex.name: Apex Intelligence
apex.focus: Autonomous research through training-stack optimization, externally reviewed projects, and scientific-autonomy evaluation.
apex.boundary: The reviewed materials substantiate research artifacts and evaluation; they do not expose continuous foundation-model self-training or a complete two-level coevolution loop.

nous.name: Nous Research
nous.focus: Persistent agent memory, skill creation, and reuse of historical experience.
nous.boundary: This entry concerns Hermes Agent's external learning mechanisms; other Nous model-training projects are separate.

intology.name: Intology
intology.focus: Locus for automated AI R&D and Zochi for scientific outputs and external review.
intology.boundary: Locus previews and the 2026 post-training report provide results, while parts of the research stack and its inherited update mechanisms remain private.

autoscience.name: Autoscience
autoscience.focus: Automated scientists and engineers organize algorithm exploration, experiments, and deployment.
autoscience.boundary: The company release was reviewed; Carl and Mira technical pages were access-limited, leaving training and cross-project inheritance incompletely disclosed.

recursive.name: Recursive / Recursive Superintelligence
recursive.focus: Automated AI R&D experiments and participation in self-evolving agent research.
recursive.boundary: First Steps and the jointly authored Agent0 paper are separate records; shared organizational participation does not establish a shared internal system.

sakana.name: Sakana AI
sakana.focus: Program evolution, self-modifying agents, and model–agent-system adaptation.
sakana.boundary: Specific papers distinguish frozen-model harness evolution from coupled model updates.

weco.name: Weco AI
weco.focus: Research agents that develop successor researchers, including tests of whether successors can take over improvement.
weco.boundary: AIDE² keeps the outer researcher fixed in its main loop; its separate ignition experiment has an inconclusive takeover result.

igent.name: iGent AI
igent.focus: SICA studies coding agents that edit their own implementation and select successors using task evaluation.
igent.boundary: SICA is the research basis; general Maestro coding features are a separate product scope.

prime-intellect.name: Prime Intellect
prime-intellect.focus: Agent harnesses, large-scale RL, verifiers, and open training infrastructure.
prime-intellect.boundary: Prime Agent and INTELLECT-3 are separate entries with different update objects; their coexistence does not establish joint autonomous evolution.

frontis.name: Frontis.AI / Horizon Research
frontis.focus: Model training and machine-learning research agents within a shared research agenda.
frontis.boundary: The Frontis-MA1 / OpenMLE entry records models, framework, and experimental results separately.

deepwisdom.name: DeepWisdom
deepwisdom.focus: Workflow search for improving multi-step agent execution.
deepwisdom.boundary: AFlow is a jointly authored study; other commercial and MetaGPT capabilities are outside that experiment.

memtensor.name: MemTensor
memtensor.focus: Accumulating task experience through external memory and learned memory utility.
memtensor.boundary: The entry follows MemRL's public mechanism, separating memory updates from foundation-model weight training.

hexo.name: Hexo Labs
hexo.focus: Model and system adaptation in the public SIA project.
hexo.boundary: The linked study supplies the applicable model-scale and source-coverage details.

iquest.name: IQuest Research
iquest.focus: ModularRSI research on organizing capabilities into evolving modules.
iquest.boundary: The affiliation links participation in a specific study, not organizational identity among all collaborators.

langboat.name: Langboat
langboat.boundary: ModularRSI is coauthored with IQuest and counted once as a work.

flower.name: Flower Labs
flower.focus: Adaptation and competitive pressure in self-modifying agents.
flower.boundary: The research link follows paper affiliation; general federated-learning products have a separate scope.

bespoke.name: Bespoke Labs
bespoke.focus: Program and prompt optimization from execution feedback and natural-language reflection.
bespoke.boundary: GEPA is a multi-institution collaboration, not an exclusive company result.

etude.name: Etude AI
etude.focus: Reward agents built with editable skills and tools.
etude.boundary: RewardHarness uses a frozen base model; downstream policy training is distinct from training the reward agent itself.

tokenwave.name: TokenWave.AI
tokenwave.focus: Automated harness development and related evaluation.
tokenwave.boundary: HarnessDev and Aspire are distinct materials; affiliation and author claims are recorded separately.

einsia.name: Einsia.AI
einsia.boundary: AI4AI-Bench supplies measurement conditions across routes; benchmark participation alone does not establish an RSI system.

deepseek.name: DeepSeek
deepseek.focus: Parameter learning, verifiable rewards, and mathematical verification feedback.
deepseek.boundary: The linked reports distinguish ordinary RL, iterative verifiers, and updates to the improvement procedure.

moonshot.name: Moonshot AI
moonshot.focus: Agentic training and synthetic experience for tool use.
moonshot.boundary: Kimi K2's training loop is described separately from execution frameworks in products.

zhipu.name: Zhipu AI
zhipu.focus: WebRL research on learning from web interaction trajectories.
zhipu.boundary: The linked work trains 8B and 9B models; company size does not change experimental model scale.

reflection.name: Reflection AI
reflection.focus: Foundation models and an agentic software stack.
reflection.boundary: Beam's model card describes 501B total and 23B active parameters and RL data sources; it does not specify an autonomous recursive-update mechanism.

miromind.name: MiroMind
miromind.focus: Agent-native training and verification-centered research agents.
miromind.boundary: The 1.7 / H1 release describes synthetic mid-training, SFT, preference optimization, RL, and verification; autonomous two-way harness evolution is not established.

field-harness-01.explanation: Retrieved experience changes the model's immediate context; persistent memory and current context are distinct states.

field-harness-02.explanation: Task interactions produce records that can be summarized and revised.

field-harness-03.explanation: Exploration packages successful operations into callable skills.

field-harness-04.explanation: New tools expand the action space; control logic chooses when to call and combine them.

field-harness-05.explanation: Workflow implementation requires calls, state, and error handling, with associated runtime costs.

field-harness-06.explanation: Execution logs, exceptions, and costs determine which failures are observable.

field-harness-07.explanation: Evaluation affects candidate retention, parent sampling, and exploration budgets.

field-harness-08.explanation: Reflection, mutation, and Pareto selection can operate on prompts.

field-harness-09.explanation: Search can change loops, roles, and model-call order.

field-harness-10.explanation: Execution and task feedback retain or repair candidate skills.

field-harness-11.explanation: Historical failures and candidates inform proposals without necessarily changing the search algorithm.

field-harness-12.explanation: An editable improver can change diagnosis and proposal methods; outer selection rules may remain fixed.

field-harness-13.explanation: The searched program can be the program that produces the next edit.

field-harness-14.explanation: Evaluate the improver's ability to produce stronger descendants within a fixed budget.

field-harness-15.explanation: Revised evaluation components change signals used by subsequent search.

field-harness-16.explanation: Lineage archives preserve intermediate candidates as future starting points.

field-harness-17.explanation: Executable skills carry reusable capabilities across tasks.

field-harness-18.explanation: Stored knowledge becomes capability through effective later use.

field-harness-19.explanation: Inherited skills make new tasks reachable and change subsequent experience.

field-harness-20.explanation: Improvement strategies can transfer alongside task programs, as tested by dedicated transfer experiments.

field-model-01.explanation: External answers or execution results determine which generated trajectories enter training.

field-model-02.explanation: Learned evaluators select or label the next generated training set.

field-model-03.explanation: Evaluation models turn open-response comparisons into preferences.

field-model-04.explanation: Shared generator–judge weights can change both abilities; judgment quality needs measurement.

field-model-05.explanation: Verifiable task outcomes train and calibrate learned critics.

field-model-06.explanation: Generated candidates supply new evaluator-training examples.

field-model-07.explanation: Task generation changes the pool from which a curriculum samples.

field-model-08.explanation: Solver performance feeds difficulty and learnability information to task generators.

field-model-09.explanation: Executable environments can validate both proposed tasks and their answers.

field-model-10.explanation: Generated tasks create new interaction trajectories.

field-model-11.explanation: Failures and capability gaps change the next curriculum.

field-model-12.explanation: Actions and execution produce verifiable state changes.

field-model-13.explanation: Selected interaction experience supports supervised replay or distillation alongside online RL.

field-model-14.explanation: An outer objective trains data-generation or self-editing policies from inner-learning gains.

field-model-15.explanation: Downstream execution trains policies that turn experience into skills or harness changes.

field-model-16.explanation: Learned update policies support adaptation on new tasks; long-term retention is a separate objective.

field-model-17.explanation: Verified test-time attempts can update parameters as well as support search.

field-model-18.explanation: AI-generated or rewritten corpora supply pretraining data; this alone is a one-way relation.

field-model-19.explanation: Learning-feedback data selection connects to pretraining mixture optimization, with DoReMi as a mechanism reference.

field-model-20.explanation: Training gains can be an outer objective for data generators or update rules; this is a research connection, not a claimed frontier-scale result.

field-hybrid-01.explanation: Workflows change the states and actions supplied to parameter learning.

field-hybrid-02.explanation: Training changes capabilities and planning styles, potentially invalidating the previous harness.

field-hybrid-03.explanation: The updated model designs another system, testing transfer from solving to improvement.

field-hybrid-04.explanation: Models propose and select roles, instructions, tool flows, and recovery strategies.

field-hybrid-05.explanation: Retrieved skills shape rollouts and supervision.

field-hybrid-06.explanation: Updated policies expose new failures and gaps in skills or memory operations.

field-hybrid-07.explanation: A designer uses failures to create curricula or environment wrappers.

field-hybrid-08.explanation: Environment and curriculum changes determine sampled states, actions, and feedback.

field-hybrid-09.explanation: Evaluation selects trajectories, assigns rewards, and constructs corrective targets.

field-hybrid-10.explanation: Policy updates change the evaluator's training distribution.

field-hybrid-11.explanation: Task difficulty affects success/failure balance and evaluator learnability.

field-hybrid-12.explanation: Disagreement between scores and behavior motivates reward, filtering, or diagnostic changes.

field-hybrid-13.explanation: Research models propose executable training code, diagnostics, and recipe edits.

field-hybrid-14.explanation: The training system determines gradient updates and retained model versions.

field-hybrid-15.explanation: Roles and communication topology become workflow-design variables.

field-hybrid-16.explanation: Execution and orchestration traces supervise shared or role-specific models.

field-hybrid-17.explanation: Research diagnostics and failures become reusable skills for future training interventions.

field-hybrid-18.explanation: Changed interfaces, tools, or model versions expose workflow mismatches.

field-hybrid-19.explanation: Internalized behavior may reduce external support, as tested in the target deployment interface.

field-hybrid-20.explanation: Training covers varied harness states or states actually visited by the student.
